sources.entry: Mox - Complete e-mail solution with IMAP4, SMTP, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, MTA-STS, DANE and DNSSEC, reputation-based and content-based junk filtering, Internationalization (IDNA), automatic TLS with ACME and Let's Encrypt, account autoconfiguration, and webmail. (Source Code) MIT Go

summary.one_liner: Mox is an MIT-licensed, self-hosted mail server written in Go that bundles SMTP, IMAP, webmail, email authentication (SPF/DKIM/DMARC), spam filtering and automatic TLS.
summary.what_it_does: Mox provides SMTP for receiving, submitting and delivering email, and IMAP4 for client access, with webmail for browser-based reading and sending. It authenticates messages and deliveries with SPF, DKIM, DMARC (including aggregate reports), DANE and MTA-STS, and supports REQUIRETLS and TLSRPT reporting. Spam handling combines per-user reputation tracking, a per-user Bayesian filter learning from Junk/Non-Junk classification, and temporary slowing of low-reputation senders, with rejected mail held in a Rejects mailbox. It obtains TLS certificates automatically via ACME (Let's Encrypt and other CAs), and includes a web admin interface for domains, accounts, aliases and DNS record instructions. Other features named include account autodiscovery, a built-in webserver/reverse proxy, an HTTP/JSON webapi and webhooks for transactional email, Prometheus metrics, and a "mox localserve" test mode.
use_cases: Self-host a mail server for my own domain
Run email for a small team or family
Send transactional email through an HTTP API
Set up IMAP and SMTP accounts with automatic TLS
Browse and send email from a web browser
Test email delivery locally during development
notable: Complete mail stack (SMTP, IMAP4, webmail, admin UI) in one binary
Reputation-based and Bayesian junk filtering learned per user
Automatic TLS via ACME with DANE and MTA-STS support
Quickstart command generates config and prints required DNS records
Built-in webserver/reverse proxy and HTTP/JSON webapi with webhooks
caveats: Only fully works on unix systems; on Windows 'mox serve' does not yet work (localserve and most subcommands do); no Plan 9 support
Modern email requires HTTPS and mox currently needs its own webserver for ACME, so a dedicated machine is recommended
Docker is described as not recommended and requires host networking; POP3 and direct maildir access are not planned
